guidelines.detail: same as LRN-108 (M1 shows the reference has a separate task for the sending step that the generated model lacks, and S1 states that send as its own sentence before the review in S2. The generated model appears to have dropped the send step or reduced it to a flow, which LRN-108 already prohibits for the receipt side. The gateway difference (M2) is weaker support: a shared end event can accept several alternative f)

same as LRN-108 (The reference has a task for the sender's sending step before the receiver's review, and the generated model lacks it (M1), although the description states it as its own sentence (S1) before the review (S2). The generated review task matches the reference review (P3), so the sending step was merged away or omitted. LRN-108 already covers the same pattern of a separately described submission or rec)

refines ACT-04 (The reference has a separate task for the initial send that the generated model omits, and the description states it as a distinct first action before the review. ACT-04 covers when to use a send task, but not that a described initial send step must be kept as its own task ahead of the review. The guideline adds that requirement. It does not contradict FID-02 or ACT-05, which it is consistent with)

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that a submitted item is then received by another party before that party decides on it, and the receipt is described as a separate step: Model the receipt as its own task, placed after the submission task and before the decision task of the receiving party, with flow running submission, then receipt, then decision. Do not drop the receipt or fold it into the submission task or the decision task.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states, in its own sentence, that one participant sends an item or notice to another participant, and the receiving participant then reviews that item as a separate step

rules_sent_back.instruction: When The description states that one participant sends or submits an item to another participant as the first step, and the other participant then reviews it.: Model the sending step as its own task of the sending participant (a send task when the send is the modeled unit of work, otherwise a task), placed before the review task and linked to it by a sequence flow. Do not drop this step or fold it into the review task, and do not replace it with an event unless the description describes waiting for a message.
rules_sent_back.situation: The description states that one participant sends or submits an item to another participant as the first step, and the other participant then reviews it.

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description states that one step is completed by one of several alternative actions, listed with 'or' or 'whether it is X, Y or Z', and the alternatives are not merged into one activity by the description: Model each alternative action as its own task placed after an exclusive gateway that splits the flow, and join the alternative tasks with an exclusive merge gateway before the next step. Do not model the alternatives as one task whose label lists all options.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description states that one participant either performs one action or another alternative action on the same item, joined by 'or', so only one of the alternatives occurs
